entries.name: Protein characterization
entries.definition: Working out a protein's identity, size, structure, purity and properties with methods such as electrophoresis and mass spectrometry.

entries.name: Protein-protein interaction
entries.definition: The physical contacts between proteins that carry out biological functions, and the methods used to detect and study them.

entries.name: Protein structure prediction
entries.definition: Predicting a protein's three-dimensional shape from its amino-acid sequence, for example with AlphaFold.

entries.name: Protocol-oriented programming
entries.definition: A programming approach, popularised by Swift, that builds behaviour from protocols and their extensions instead of from class inheritance.

entries.name: Prototype JavaScript Framework
entries.definition: A JavaScript framework that extends the browser's built-in objects with helpers for working with the page, Ajax requests and class-like inheritance.

entries.name: Prototyping
entries.definition: Building representations to explore and test a proposed system.

entries.name: Protractor
entries.definition: An end-to-end test framework for Angular and AngularJS web apps that drives a real browser through Selenium WebDriver.

entries.name: Data provenance
entries.definition: Tracing data and claims to their sources and transformations.

entries.name: PTAS reduction
entries.definition: A reduction between optimisation problems that preserves the existence of a polynomial-time approximation scheme, used to compare how well problems can be approximated.

entries.name: Public history
entries.definition: The practice of presenting history to general audiences, in places such as museums, archives, historic sites and the media.

entries.name: Public-key cryptography
entries.definition: Cryptography in which each user has a public key that anyone can use to encrypt or verify and a private key kept secret to decrypt or sign.

entries.name: Public-Key Cryptography Standards
entries.definition: A set of numbered specifications, first published by RSA Laboratories, that define formats and interfaces for public-key cryptography, such as PKCS #1 for RSA.

entries.name: Public policy
entries.definition: The laws, rules and government actions that address public problems, and the study of how they are made and what effects they have.

entries.name: Pug
entries.definition: A template engine for Node.js and browsers that compiles indentation-based templates into HTML.

entries.name: Punctuation
entries.definition: Using punctuation marks correctly so that written text is clear.

entries.name: PuPHPet
entries.definition: A web-based tool that generates Vagrant and Puppet configuration for setting up PHP development environments.

entries.name: Puppet
entries.definition: A configuration-management tool in which the desired state of servers is described in a declarative language and then enforced automatically.

entries.name: Puppeteer
entries.definition: A Node.js library from the Chrome team that controls Chrome or Chromium through code, often for browser testing and automation.

entries.name: PuTTY
entries.definition: A free terminal program, first made for Windows, that connects to remote machines over SSH, Telnet and serial lines.

entries.name: PyMongo
entries.definition: The official Python driver for working with MongoDB databases.

entries.name: PyTables
entries.definition: A Python library for managing large hierarchical datasets, built on the HDF5 file format and NumPy.

entries.name: Python for data analysis
entries.definition: Using Python and libraries such as pandas and NumPy to clean, explore and analyse data.

entries.name: Python Server Pages
entries.definition: A way of embedding Python code in HTML pages so that a web server runs it to produce the page, much as PHP and JavaServer Pages do.

entries.name: Python Tools for Visual Studio
entries.definition: A free, open-source extension that adds Python editing, debugging and project support to Microsoft Visual Studio.

entries.name: PyTorch
entries.definition: Building and training tensor-based machine-learning models with PyTorch.

entries.name: QARun
entries.definition: A Compuware tool for recording, scripting and replaying automated tests of an application's user interface.

entries.name: Qlik Sense
entries.definition: A data analytics and business-intelligence platform from Qlik for building interactive dashboards and exploring data.

entries.name: QlikView
entries.definition: An in-memory business-intelligence tool from Qlik for building interactive dashboards and reports.

entries.name: QS/1
entries.definition: Pharmacy management software used to handle prescriptions, billing and inventory in a pharmacy.

entries.name: Qualitative data analysis
entries.definition: Examining non-numerical data such as interview transcripts, field notes and open-ended answers to find themes and meaning.

entries.name: Quantitative models of the action potential
entries.definition: Mathematical models, such as the Hodgkin-Huxley model, that describe how a nerve cell's membrane voltage changes during an action potential.

entries.name: Quantum dot
entries.definition: A semiconductor crystal a few nanometres across whose size sets the colour of light it emits and absorbs.

entries.name: Quantum Merlin Arthur
entries.definition: A computational complexity class of decision problems whose yes answers a quantum computer can check from a quantum proof of reasonable size, the quantum counterpart of NP.

entries.name: Quantum spin Hall effect
entries.definition: A state of matter in which a material's interior is an electrical insulator while its edges carry currents of electrons whose spin direction depends on the direction they travel.

entries.name: Quartile
entries.definition: One of three values that divide a sorted set of data into four equal-sized groups.

entries.name: Queer theory
entries.definition: An academic field, emerging in the early 1990s, that examines how categories of sexuality and gender are made and challenged in culture and society.

entries.name: Question answering
entries.definition: The natural language processing task in which a system gives answers to questions asked in everyday language.

entries.name: Queue management system
entries.definition: A system that issues tickets to customers, puts them in order and shows who is called next, as in banks, clinics and service offices.

entries.name: QuickTime VR
entries.definition: An Apple technology within QuickTime for viewing panoramic images and object movies interactively.

entries.name: Qumu
entries.definition: An enterprise video platform for creating, managing and streaming video inside organisations, from Qumu Corporation.
